original_failed_run.failed_job: Build, lint, test, warehouse file checks

root_cause: 8 real ESLint/React-Compiler errors in 4 component files: react-hooks/static-components (StrategyForm.tsx CharCount declared inside render), react-hooks/rules-of-hooks (SavedReportClient.tsx two useMemo after 5 early returns), react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization (ComparePropertiesClient.tsx resultA/resultB referenced via closure before their useMemo declarations), react-hooks/refs (AnalysePropertyClient.tsx ref read during render).
why_local_checks_were_misleading: npm run lint correctly reported these 8 errors every time it was run locally throughout Sprint 11 -- the tool output was never wrong. The mistake was interpretation: because all 4 files were last touched by an ancestor commit (ebc6552) predating Sprint 11, prior reports treated the errors as pre-existing/unrelated and therefore acceptable. That is a true statement about origin but a false implication about CI outcome -- GitHub Actions checks exit code on the current tree with no continue-on-error, it has no concept of whose commit introduced a bug. Cross-checking gh run list showed CI had failed on every run since the workflow was created (20b248e, WS15) through a713931 -- 10 consecutive failing runs, never green, the entire time Sprint 11's reports described the codebase as passing.

reproduction.method: disposable git worktree (git worktree add --detach) at commit a713931, containing no node_modules/.env.local/warehouse-data, verified clean before running anything
reproduction.node_version_used: 20.19.0 (portable download, matching CI's actions/setup-node node-version: 20 exactly; local dev machine runs Node 24)
